label: Final Act of the Congress of Vienna
why: The Final Act settles Europe after Napoleon, nine days before Waterloo, while Spanish America fights for independence and Britain rules India.

realms.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland
realms.note: Map id england; Great Britain from 1707; Union with Ireland 1 Jan 1801. Rules India through the East India Company and holds Java, Malacca, the Cape, Ceylon and Malta.

realms.name: French Empire (Hundred Days)
realms.note: Napoleon rules again from 20 March to 22 June 1815; the Bourbon Louis XVIII waits in Ghent. Waterloo follows on 18 June.

realms.name: Austrian Empire
realms.note: Includes Hungary, Bohemia, Galicia and, from 7 Apr 1815, the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia.

realms.name: Kingdom of Prussia
realms.note: Map id brandenburg; gains the Rhineland, Westphalia and northern Saxony at Vienna.

realms.name: Russian Empire
realms.note: Map id muscovy; holds Finland (1809), Bessarabia (1812), Georgia and the Duchy of Warsaw under provisional rule.

realms.name: Kingdom of Spain
realms.note: Map id castile; restored absolutism 1814; its American empire is at war with independence movements.

realms.name: Kingdom of Portugal
realms.note: The court sits in Rio de Janeiro since 1808; Lisbon is run by a regency council. The United Kingdom with Brazil is proclaimed in Dec 1815.

realms.name: United Kingdom of the Netherlands
realms.note: Joins the former Dutch Republic and the Austrian Netherlands; confirmed by the Final Act.

realms.name: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
realms.note: Created by the Final Act in personal union with the Netherlands; member of the German Confederation.

realms.name: Kingdom of Sweden
realms.ruler: Charles XIII (Crown Prince Charles John governs)
realms.note: Lost Finland 1809; gained Norway in union 1814.

realms.name: Kingdom of Norway
realms.note: Personal union with Sweden from 4 Nov 1814 under its own constitution.

realms.name: Kingdom of Denmark
realms.note: Lost Norway by the Treaty of Kiel (Jan 1814); keeps Iceland, the Faroes, Greenland, Schleswig and Holstein.

realms.name: Kingdom of Sardinia
realms.note: House of Savoy (map id savoy); gains the former Republic of Genoa (1815).

realms.name: Kingdom of Naples and Sicily
realms.ruler: Ferdinand IV of Naples / III of Sicily
realms.note: Two crowns in personal union until merged as the Two Sicilies in Dec 1816. Murat fell in May 1815; Austrian troops took Naples for Ferdinand on 23 May.

realms.name: Papal States
realms.note: Pius VII came back to Rome on 7 June 1815 after fleeing Murat's advance.

realms.name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
realms.note: Successor of the Republic of Florence (map id florence); Habsburg-Lorraine restored 1814.

realms.name: Duchy of Modena
realms.note: Este duchy; catalogue record is the 1444 Este state (Ferrara-Modena).

realms.name: Duchy of Parma
realms.note: Assigned to Napoleon's wife by the Final Act; she stays in Vienna for now.

realms.name: Swiss Confederation
realms.ruler: Federal Diet (Landammann Hans von Reinhard of Zürich)
realms.note: 22 cantons; neutrality recognised at Vienna; Federal Treaty signed Aug 1815.

realms.name: Kingdom of Saxony
realms.note: King back in Dresden on 7 June 1815 after Prussian-Russian occupation; lost about half its land to Prussia.

realms.name: Kingdom of Hanover
realms.note: Brunswick-Lüneburg raised to a kingdom in Oct 1814; personal union with Britain.

realms.name: Mecklenburg-Schwerin
realms.note: Raised to a grand duchy by the Final Act.

realms.name: Free City of Kraków
realms.ruler: Organising committee under the three partitioning powers
realms.note: Created by the treaties of 3 May 1815 and the Final Act; its institutions were set up later in 1815.

realms.name: Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro
realms.note: De facto independent; Ottomans claim it.

realms.name: Pashalik of Yanina
realms.note: Ali Pasha rules Epirus and much of Greece as an autonomous Ottoman governor.

realms.name: Shirvan Khanate
realms.note: Under Russian suzerainty since 1805; Gulistan 1813.

realms.name: Regency of Algiers
realms.note: Nominal Ottoman suzerainty; at war with the United States (Second Barbary War) since Mar 1815.

realms.name: Beylik of Tunis
realms.note: Husainid beys; nominal Ottoman suzerainty.

realms.name: Eyalet of Egypt (Muhammad Ali)
realms.note: Governor since 1805; massacred the Mamluks 1811; occupies the Hejaz for the Sultan against the Saudis.

realms.name: Mamluk Pashalik of Baghdad
realms.note: Georgian Mamluk governors, largely autonomous.

realms.name: Emirate of Diriyah (First Saudi State)
realms.note: Lost the Hejaz to Egypt 1812-13; destroyed 1818.

realms.name: Sultanate of Muscat and Oman
realms.note: Holds Zanzibar and the Swahili coast and leases Bandar Abbas and Hormuz from Persia.

realms.name: Sultanate of Lahej
realms.note: Abdali sultans, independent of the imam since 1728; hold Aden.

realms.name: Qajar Iran
realms.note: Lost Georgia and the northern khanates to Russia (Gulistan 1813).

realms.name: Durrani Empire
realms.note: Fragmenting; Herat under Mahmud's brother Firuz al-Din, Kashmir under Azim Khan.

realms.name: Talpur Sindh
realms.ruler: Mir Karam Ali Talpur (with his brothers)

realms.name: Mughal Empire
realms.note: A pensioner of the East India Company since 1803; rules little beyond the Red Fort.

realms.name: Maratha Peshwa (Pune)
realms.note: Bound by the subsidiary Treaty of Bassein (1802); the confederacy is ending.

realms.name: Holkar of Indore
realms.ruler: Malhar Rao Holkar III (regent Tulsi Bai)

realms.name: Puar of Dhar
realms.note: Small Maratha state wasted by Pindaris and Scindia.

realms.name: Kingdom of Nepal
realms.ruler: Girvan Yuddha Bikram Shah (Bhimsen Thapa governs)
realms.note: At war with the East India Company since Nov 1814.

realms.name: Ahom Kingdom
realms.note: Weak; Burmese invasions begin 1817.

realms.name: Tibet (Ganden Phodrang)
realms.ruler: Regent Demo Tulku (9th Dalai Lama died Mar 1815)

realms.name: Joseon
realms.note: Tributary of the Qing.

realms.name: Tokugawa Shogunate
realms.ruler: Shogun Tokugawa Ienari (Emperor Kōkaku in Kyoto)

realms.name: Ryukyu Kingdom
realms.note: Under Satsuma since 1609 and a Qing tributary.

realms.name: Kingdom of Siam (Rattanakosin)
realms.note: Successor of Ayutthaya (map id ayutthaya).

realms.name: Kingdom of Cambodia
realms.note: Under Vietnamese protection since 1813; Siam holds the northwest.

realms.name: Sultanate of Johor-Riau
realms.note: Succession disputed since 1812; the Temenggong holds Singapore island.

realms.name: Sultanate of Ternate
realms.note: British occupation of the Moluccas 1810-1817 in place of the Dutch.

realms.name: Sokoto Caliphate
realms.ruler: Usman dan Fodio (Muhammad Bello governs the east)

realms.name: Bornu
realms.ruler: Mai Dunama IX (Shehu Muhammad al-Amin al-Kanemi holds power)

realms.name: Tuareg overlordship of Timbuktu
realms.ruler: Tuareg chiefs over the Arma pashas (names uncertain)
realms.note: Arma pashalik reduced to a tributary of the Tuareg; Massina takes the city c.1826.

realms.name: Oyo Empire
realms.note: In decline before the Ilorin revolt of 1817.

realms.name: Ethiopian Empire
realms.ruler: Egwale Seyon (Ras Gugsa of Yejju holds power)
realms.note: Zemene Mesafint: the emperor is a figurehead.

realms.name: Rozvi State
realms.note: In decline before the Nguni invasions of the 1830s.

realms.name: United States
realms.note: The War of 1812 ended with the Treaty of Ghent (ratified Feb 1815).

realms.name: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
realms.note: Independence declared only in July 1816.

realms.name: Federal League (Artigas)
realms.note: Holds the Banda Oriental (Montevideo since Feb 1815) and the Littoral provinces against Buenos Aires.

realms.name: Paraguay
realms.ruler: José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia (Supreme Dictator)

realms.name: United Provinces of New Granada
realms.ruler: Executive triumvirate of the Congress (members uncertain)
realms.note: Spanish reconquest under Morillo lands Apr 1815; Bogotá falls in May 1816.

realms.name: Supreme Mexican Government (insurgents)
realms.ruler: José María Morelos and the insurgent Congress
realms.note: Constitution of Apatzingán (Oct 1814); a moving seat in Michoacán; Morelos is captured in Nov 1815.

realms.name: Sultanate of Aceh
realms.ruler: Jauhar al-Alam Syah (contested by Saiful Alam)
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Jaipur State (Amber)
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Pashalik of Timbuktu (Arma)
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Nominal; Tuareg dominate Timbuktu. Ended by Massina 1826–1833.

realms.name: Bhutan (Drukpa state)
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Sultanate of Brunei
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Thuận Thành (Champa remnant)
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Abolished 1832.

realms.name: Kingdom of Champasak
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Sultanate of Gowa (Makassar)
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Dutch suzerainty, under the British interregnum 1811–1816.

realms.name: Sharifate of Mecca
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Under Muhammad Ali's Egypt since 1813.

realms.name: Kingdom of Hungary
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Own diet and laws within the Austrian Empire.

realms.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Crown land of the Austrian Empire.

realms.name: Kazakh Khanate
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Fragmented into the three juz under Russian pressure; khans abolished 1822–1824.

calais.note: Under Napoleon in the Hundred Days.

bordeaux.note: Under Napoleon in the Hundred Days. The Duchess of Angoulême's royalist stand ended in early April.

paris.note: Under Napoleon in the Hundred Days.

rouen.note: Under Napoleon in the Hundred Days.

nantes.note: Imperial garrison; the Vendée rose for the king in May-June 1815.

dijon.note: Under Napoleon in the Hundred Days.

marseille.note: Royalist city held for Napoleon by Marshal Brune; it rises on 25 June.

brussels.note: Wellington's army is gathered around it.

lisbon.note: Governed by a regency while the court is in Rio de Janeiro.

genoa.note: Former Republic of Genoa given to Sardinia; Sardinian rule from Jan 1815.

naples.note: Murat fled in May; Austrian troops entered for Ferdinand IV on 23 May and the king returns in June.

palermo.note: Kingdom of Sicily, same king; the court sat here 1806-1815.

dresden.note: Prussian-Russian occupation ended; the king returned on 7 June 1815.

cologne.note: Rhine lands taken over by Prussia in April 1815.

oslo.note: Christiania; Norway in union with Sweden.

krakow.note: Free City created by the treaties of 3 May and the Final Act; Russian troops still held it on the day, and its government was set up later in 1815.

buda.note: Kingdom of Hungary within the Austrian Empire.

belgrade.note: Ottoman fortress; the Second Serbian Uprising under Miloš Obrenović began in April 1815.

tabriz.note: Seat of Crown Prince Abbas Mirza.

baghdad.note: Mamluk pasha under nominal Ottoman rule.

mecca.note: Egyptian occupation since 1813; Sharif Yahya ibn Surur installed by Muhammad Ali.

hormuz.note: Leased with Bandar Abbas from Persia by the Muscat sultans.

herat.note: Held by the Sadozai prince Firuz al-Din, nearly independent and paying tribute to Persia at times.

delhi.note: Delhi Territory run by the Company's Resident; the Mughal Akbar II reigns only in the Red Fort.

ahmedabad.note: City shared by the Peshwa and the Gaekwad; the Peshwa's lease of his half to Baroda lapsed in 1814. Could be scored as baroda.

mandu.note: Part of Dhar, a small Maratha state; Malwa overrun by Scindia, Holkar and the Pindaris.

vijayanagara.note: Bellary district, ceded to the Company in 1800.

colombo.note: Crown colony; Kandy annexed in Mar 1815.

karakorum.note: Khalkha Mongolia under Qing banner rule.

hakata.note: Fukuoka domain of the Kuroda under the shogunate.

angkor.note: Siem Reap, held by Siam since 1795.

malacca.note: British occupation 1795-1818; returned to the Dutch in 1818.

ternate.note: Sultan under British occupation in place of the Dutch.

timbuktu.note: Arma pashas under Tuareg tribute; no strong state.

gao.note: Iwellemmeden Tuareg and Songhay remnants; no state.

niani.note: Small Maninka kafus of the upper Niger; no state.

kanem.note: Kanem contested between Bornu and Wadai.

kilwa.note: Omani governor over the local sultan.

mogadishu.note: Somali clan elders; Geledi sultanate influence; Omani claims only.

zeila.note: Dependency of Mocha under the Zaydi imam, as usually reported.

gondar.note: Figurehead emperor; Ras Gugsa of Yejju rules.

cape.note: Cape Colony; ceded by the Dutch in 1814.

tzintzuntzan.note: Michoacán, where Morelos's insurgent government moves about.

cusco.note: Royalists retook it after Pumacahua's rising (Mar 1815).

bogota.note: Morillo's expedition is landing in Venezuela; Bogotá falls in May 1816.

singapore.note: Temenggong Abdul Rahman of Johor settled there in 1811; British founding in 1819.

open_questions: Realm ids follow the sibling checkpoints (1600, 1914): successor states keep the map id of their core (england for the United Kingdom, muscovy for Russia, castile for Spain, brandenburg for Prussia, savoy for Sardinia, florence for Tuscany, luneburg for Hanover, ayutthaya for Siam, ava for Burma, dai_viet for Nguyễn Vietnam, khmer for Cambodia, vientiane for Vientiane (lan_xang is Luang Prabang), persia for Qajar Iran, haiti for Pétion's republic). The formed and ended lists were recomputed against 1715.json in the id harmonisation (dutch_republic is netherlands).
Kraków: the Free City is created on paper by the 3 May treaties and the Final Act, but Russian troops held it on 9 June and its government came later; russia is a fair alternative holder.
Congress Poland is created by the Final Act but proclaimed only on 20 June 1815, so it is not listed; the Duchy of Warsaw is under Russian provisional rule.
Naples: Austrian troops held the city for Ferdinand IV from 23 May; the date of Ferdinand's own return in June is uncertain. Naples and Sicily are counted as one realm (merged Dec 1816).
Ahmedabad was split between the Peshwa and the Gaekwad; the status of the Peshwa's half after the 1814 lease lapsed is uncertain.

Delhi and other Company lands are scored as united_kingdom (colonial power), not as a separate East India Company realm; the Mughal emperor and the subsidiary-alliance princes are given the United Kingdom as overlord.
West Africa: Timbuktu, Gao and Niani have no clear state; the Oyo Alaafin, the Rozvi Changamire, the Ternate sultan and the New Granada triumvirate are not named with confidence.
Mogadishu and Zeila: local rule is poorly documented; Zeila's dependence on Mocha (Yemen) is the usual account.
Kanem: contested between Bornu and Wadai around 1815.
France on this date is Napoleon's Hundred Days regime; the Bourbon kingdom is restored on 8 July 1815. The same id france is used for both.

Id harmonisation: the Kingdom of Vientiane uses vientiane (lan_xang is Luang Prabang, added here); the UK uses england, Hanover luneburg, the Maratha Peshwa maratha, Russia muscovy, Qing jurchens, Qajar Iran persia, the Durrani state afghanistan, the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata argentina, the Emirate of Bukhara uzbek_khanate and Sennar funj.

Thirty realms standing in June 1815 were added from the 1715 list (among them Hungary and Bohemia as Habsburg crown kingdoms, Sicily until the union of December 1816, Jaipur, Mewar, Marwar, Travancore, Bhutan, Brunei, Aceh, Sulu, Mossi, Mapuche, Khalkha under the Qing). Tibet (Ganden Phodrang) reuses the map id tibet and is counted as formed; Phagmodrupa ended before 1715.
Lucca is counted as ended (republic gone 1799/1805; the Bourbon duchy only takes over in 1817), the Iroquois as ended as a sovereign confederacy after the American Revolution.
